key_insight: Among four WC-10Co-4Cr thermal-spray coatings, HVAF delivered the lowest measured wear rate and best corrosion resistance, while HVOF had the highest hardness.
engineering_relevance: HVAF is a promising coating route for 304 stainless steel components requiring combined wear and corrosion protection.
method: Deposited WC-10Co-4Cr on 304 stainless steel using APS, detonation spraying, HVOF and HVAF.
Compared microstructure, Vickers hardness, friction, volumetric wear and corrosion behavior.
Identified abrasive and fatigue wear as the main coating wear mechanisms.
evidence_signal: HVAF's wear rate was (1.10±0.01)×10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m), versus (36.82±0.80)×10⁻⁵ for uncoated steel; corrosion resistance ranked HVAF > detonation > HVOF > APS.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or corrosion medium, limiting direct transfer of these rankings to service environments.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
